thread.title: Project Snapshot Summary
thread.preview:
Yep — **procedural segments + cover rules** is the right “big next” step. The nice part: your project already has the *pieces*:

- `ChunkManager.gd` already generates **small buildings + ruins** and already spawns `CoverFull / CoverWindow / CoverHalf`.
- Threat already scales enemies/spawns, so “stop-hoarding” can mostly be a **Threat curve + spikes** problem, not a brand-new system.

So now it’s mostly: **make cover mean something**, then **make Segment 2 a generator that produces a forward escape path**.

---

## How I’d define cover (simple, readable, actually fun)

### Cover Types (2D-friendly)
**Full cover (walls):**
- Blocks movement ✅
- Blocks bullets ✅ (projectiles die on hit)
- Good for “hard LoS breaks”

**Window / 3⁄4 cover (shoot-through):**
- Blocks movement ✅
- Bullets pass through ✅ (projectiles do NOT die)
- Optional: bullets can pass but do **reduced damage** (if you want it to *feel* like cover even though it’s shoot-through)

**Half cover (tables/rubble):**
Pick ONE rule (don’t overcomplicate early):
- **Option 1 (my default): “chance to stop bullets”** (ex: 50% block)
- Option 2: “bullets pass but deal -30% damage”
- Option 3: “bullets pass but lose speed / lifetime”

**Why chance-to-block works well in horde/bullet games:** it’s immediately legible and creates “sometimes saved me” moments.

### AI doesn’t need “use cover” yet
Even if enemies don’t consciously path to cover, the battlefield gets interesting just from:
- you weaving through cover
- bullets being filtered differently by cover types

That’s a huge payoff for small code.

---

## How to implement cover without a big refactor
The lowest-risk path is:

1) Add groups to cover scenes:
- `CoverFull` → group `cover_full`
- `CoverWindow` → group `cover_window`
- `CoverHalf` → group `cover_half`

2) Update projectile collision code:
- If `cover_window`: **ignore hit**
- If `cover_half`: either **50% kill projectile** or **reduce damage**
- If `cover_full`: **kill projectile**

That alone instantly makes:
- windows shoot-through,
- half cover partial,
- walls hard blockers.

(And it’ll apply to both enemy projectiles and your ranged attacks if we update both.)

---

## Procedural segments (how to make it “escape”, not “random soup”)

### The key rule: **always generate a forward route**
Instead of pure open-world streaming, do:

- Segment has a **forward vector** (e.g. +X)
- Define a **finish distance** (e.g. 6–10 chunks)
- Place the Exit Rite at the “end band”
- Place wardstones every N chunks (like checkpoints)

Then ChunkManager can still generate buildings/ruins inside each chunk, but the *macro structure* is:
- start → checkpoint → checkpoint → gate

That makes it feel like “escaping through districts” instead of “circling forever”.

### Risk pockets (your Slay-the-Spire vibe inside the action)
Within the lane, occasionally generate a side pocket chunk flagged “risk”:
- more loot / chest / elite
- but higher threat spike or extra wave

So the player chooses: detour or push forward.

---

## “Stop-hoarding items” mechanic (you’re already 80% there)
Threat already scales:
- normal enemy stats
- spawn rate
- elite chance

To make hoarding *actually bite*, you want Threat to have:
1) **non-linear item scaling** (so going from 20 → 40 items hurts more than 0 → 20)
2) **spikes** when you pick up high rarity items (immediate consequence)

Example behavior:
- Threat = base_from_followers + base_from_items + **heat**
- Heat increases on pickup (rarity-weighted), then slowly decays
- This makes “grab shiny thing” feel like “the world noticed”

That also creates a natural incentive to sell between segments.

---

## The only design choice I need from you (and I can default it)
For **half cover**, which do you want?

1) **50% chance to block bullets** (my default)  
2) Bullets always pass but **-30% damage**  
3) Bullets always pass but **lose speed/lifetime**

If you say “default”, I’ll do #1.

---

When you’re ready, we can implement in this order (fast feedback):
1) Cover groups + projectile rules (windows shoot-through, half cover partial)  
2) Segment 2 Builder: forward lane + gate distance + wardstone intervals (reusing ChunkManager)  
3) Threat spikes / non-linear item scaling (anti-hoard that feels intentional)

Say which half-cover option you want, and I’ll start coding with a zip update.

items.text:
Yep — I can keep working on the next thing without turning into a code-parrot. No “token limit doom spiral” here.

You’ve got a solid spine now (campaign attempt + hub + threat + HUD). The next work is mostly **new systems**, not rewriting what’s already stable, so it’s the *best* time to keep building.

## What should be next (my recommendation)
Pick one of these “next pillars” — I’ll drive whichever you choose:

### A) Procedural Segment 2 (lane-chunk generator)
**Goal:** Segment 2 feels new every run but still has clear “escape direction.”
- Generate a forward route of chunks (street → courtyard → alley → plaza)
- Place: wardstones, risk pockets, and gate at the end
- Reuse your existing ChunkManager + FlowFieldNav
- Keep Level 1 handcrafted; Level 2 becomes your procedural testbed

### B) Anti-hoarding mechanic (without feeling like rubber-banding)
You already have Threat scaling enemies/spawns, but item hoarding can still become “infinite stacking.”
Add one more lever that’s *diegetic*:
- **Encumbrance / Synthesis Load**: every item past N adds:
  - slower pickup magnet, or
  - reduced healing, or
  - increases curse intensity, or
  - increases threat gain rate (cleanest—feeds your existing system)
This makes “keep stacking” a choice, not always correct.

### C) Real RPG Sell Screen
Selectable items, prices, totals, confirm, sell-from-bag or equipped.
Mostly UI work, low risk, high polish.

## My vote
**A (Procedural Segment 2)** first, because it unlocks “campaign feeling” immediately.  
Threat is now meaningful; it’s more fun when you have new spaces to run through.

## One tiny question so I build the right generator
For Segment 2: do you want it to be…
1) **Mostly outdoors** (streets/ruins), or  
2) **Mixed** (some interior chunks too), or  
3) **Theme per segment** (seg2 outdoors, seg3 sewers, etc.)

Reply with **A/B/C** + your theme choice, and I’ll start with a step-by-step implementation plan and code you can drop straight into your project.

items.text:
Implemented ✅ (in your **0.0.0.09c** project): **custom Threat tooltip scene + hover behavior**, removed the inline detail label so the HUD stays narrow, and gave the Threat bar a better “synthetic heresy” color.

:chatgpt-content-reference{index="0"}[Download the updated zip](sandbox:/mnt/data/syntethic-ascension0.0.0.09d_threat_tooltip.zip)

### What changed

#### New files
- `res://ui/widgets/ThreatTooltip.tscn`
- `res://ui/widgets/ThreatTooltip.gd`

A small styled panel (dark glass + border) with a label, meant to be spawned by the controller.

#### Updated controller
- `res://ui/controllers/HudThreatController.gd`
  - Spawns the tooltip on hover over the Threat row (default target is the whole row).
  - Tooltip follows the mouse and clamps to the viewport.
  - Keeps the “detail” text out of the HUD layout to prevent widening.

#### HUD changes
- `res://ui/screens/HUD.tscn`
  - Removed the `ThreatDetail` node (the thing that was stretching the HUD).
  - Added a new `StyleThreatBarFill` and applied it to `ThreatBar` so it’s no longer gray.
  - Wired `ThreatController.tooltip_scene` to `ThreatTooltip.tscn`, and `tooltip_target_path` to the Threat row.

### Want the Threat bar color tweaked?
Change it here:
- `res://ui/screens/HUD.tscn` → `StyleThreatBarFill.bg_color`

If you want, tell me the vibe (more “neon cyan”, more “warning red”, more “arcane purple”) and I’ll tune the exact color + tooltip styling to match the rest of your UI.
